output.summary: The record FY2026 result is mostly a commodity price effect: bushels were flat (-0.9%), grain merchandising gains drove the margin, and the cooperative ranks only 8th and 10th of 23 peers, none of which adopted a program. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes from maintenance cut from $905K to $612K while the deferred backlog tripled to $1.26M, so it reflects deferral, not efficiency. Harlan Junction has critical dust and monitoring findings with a 21 Nov insurer deadline, and the 14 July near-miss was closed without the required investigation. Staff do report concerns, but little changes. The Superintendent is a single point of failure with no successor. The expansion case rests on FY2026 prices and unsourced throughput growth. Fix the hazards, build succession, and rebuild the case before voting.
